content: The United Nations Population Fund published a report in 2013 addressing global population issues. Salam RA, Faqah A, Sajjad N, Lassi ZS, Das JK, Kaufman M, and colleagues conducted a systematic review in 2016 on potential interventions to improve adolescent sexual and reproductive health, which was published in the Journal of Adolescent Health (Volume 59, Supplement 4, Pages S11–S28). Similarly, Kalamar AM, Lee-Rife S, and Hindin MJ reviewed interventions aimed at preventing child marriage among young people in lowand middle-income countries, with their findings published in the Journal of Adolescent Health in 2016 (Volume 59, Supplement 3, Pages S16–S21). Chae S and Ngo T examined the global evidence on interventions to prevent child marriage, with their findings published by the Population Council in 2017. Shell-Duncan B, Naik R, and Feldman-Jacobs C synthesized the state of knowledge on female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C) in a report published by the Population Council in 2016. Another report by Shell-Duncan B, Njue C, and Moore Z in 2017 explored the medicalization of FGM/C, analyzing available data. Muteshi JK, Miller S, and Belizán JM highlighted the ongoing violence against women through FGM/C in their 2016 publication in Reproductive Health (Volume 13, Article 44). Arthur M, Earle A, Raub A, Vincent I, Atabay E, Latz I, and colleagues analyzed child marriage laws worldwide, focusing on minimum marriage age, legal exceptions, and gender disparities, with their findings published in the Journal of Women, Politics & Policy in 2018 (Volume 39, Issue 1, Pages 51–74). The Southern African Development Community Parliamentary Forum released the Model Law on Eradicating Child Marriage and Protecting Children Already in Marriage in 2016, based in Johannesburg. In 2014, the United Nations published a joint general recommendation (No. 31) by the Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women and a general comment (No. 18) by the Committee on the Rights of the Child, addressing harmful practices. The World Health Organization (WHO) developed a teacher’s guide in 2001 to integrate the prevention and management of FGM/C-related health complications into nursing and midwifery curricula. Additionally, WHO issued an interagency statement in 2008 on eliminating FGM and, in 2010, launched a global strategy to stop healthcare providers from performing FGM. In 2018, the National Assembly of Zambia published the outcome document of a parliamentary seminar aimed at mobilizing parliamentarians to take action to end child, early, and forced marriage.
